situation:
You are the channel manager at HALFTIME FUEL CO., a two-year-old company that makes recovery drinks for school and amateur athletes. The founder (judge) has asked you to recommend where the company's product should be sold over the coming year, and to explain what that choice would say about the brand.

HALFTIME FUEL sells directly to customers online and through SUMMIT COURTS, a chain of thirty community sports complexes. The company signed a one-year agreement promising SUMMIT COURTS that the drink would be sold in no other venue in the region, and seven months of that year remain. The first round of funding is nearly spent, and roughly four months of cash is left.

GRANDSTAND CONCESSIONS, the vendor that stocks the coolers at the region's college and minor-league stadiums, has offered to carry the drink in every one of those coolers beginning next month. The volume would cover payroll into next year. Those stadiums sit inside the region the agreement covers, so the company cannot accept without breaking the exclusivity clause, and SUMMIT COURTS could cancel and pull the drink from all thirty complexes.

To wait out the remaining seven months would keep the complexes and the athletes who already know the brand, but it leaves the company with four months of cash and no stadium shelf, and the vendor would fill that cooler space with a competitor. In a stadium cooler the drink also sits beside national brands, where nothing on the package tells a buyer what the company stands for.

The founder (judge) wants you to explain how the company should choose its channels, identify the market each channel reaches, and say what the customers in it want that they have not asked for out loud. The founder (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the founder (judge) of HALFTIME FUEL CO. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You started the company two years ago and you sign every agreement it enters. You want to hear which channels the drink should be sold through over the coming year, which market each of those channels reaches, what the choice would say about where the brand stands next to the national names, and what those customers need that they have never said out loud.

During the presentation you will ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: If we turn the vendor down, what does that cost us?
What would we be giving up by leaving the complexes?
